_provenance.why: published-replays.json's provenance is exactly 'linked from the ARC blog post', and that claim is only worth something if every row in the file satisfies it. These rows do not: they were played on our side and are not in the blog's 250. Folding them in would have made the larger file's one-line provenance false for every one of them, so they live here instead. HIGH VALUE FOR THE CORPUS: this run is the reason cn04's level-5 mechanic is now documented. ACTION5 rotates the held part across the whole of levels 1-4, and on level 5's yellow part it never rotates at all -- it steps up a 5-deep stack of nested growing variants, and the smaller variants carry fewer marks (3 at starting size, 7 fully expanded), so marks that must be satisfied are absent from the board until the part is expanded. Verified against docs/static/games/src/cn04-2fe56bfb/cn04.py:1066-1075 (ACTION5 branch), :843-858 (stack grouping by shared anchor), :1111-1135 (the cycle), :677-775 (level table). That is a rule INVERSION with no on-screen warning, which is exactly the falsified-prediction material the decision-step corpus exists to capture.

levels_completed maps from the inventory's field name 'levels' -- same value, different key. The key here matches published-replays.json, which is the shape that must not drift.

fields.game_id: the environment id, e.g. bp35-0a0ad940 -- needed to build the recordings URL
fields.levels_completed: levels completed in the run; the field is named 'levels' in the scorecard inventory and 'levels_completed' in /api/sessions
fields.resets: how many times the run was reset
fields.published_at: when the run's scorecard was published
